newsitem.title: JAPAN: Aramco naphtha to be bid below $10.00 - traders.
newsitem.headline: Aramco naphtha to be bid below $10.00 - traders.

text.p: Naphtha buyers in Japan and South Korea are expected to bid below $10.00 per tonne over the Aramco formula for Saudi Arabia's A-180 naphtha in the initial round of bidding, traders said on Friday.

Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil firm Saudi Aramco late last month asked prospective naphtha buyers in Asia to submit their bids by Friday for cargoes to be lifted in the second half of 1997. The bids will be valid until May 21.
Most firms are expected to notify Aramco of their bids late this evening, traders said.

One trader with a petrochemical firm in South Korea said he believes a premium of $7.00 to $8.00 is a reasonable bidding level, while a Japanese trader with a trading house said the firm has not decided on the bidding price, but it will definitely be below $10.00.

Meanwhile, Saudi Aramco is expected to be targeting a double-digit premium on the back of region's growing appetite for naphtha as petrochemical feedstock, traders said. The current premium for A-180 was set at $6.50 for the first half of 1997.

Reflecting the growing regional naphtha demand, Kuwait Petroleum Corp's naphtha in February successfully fetched the term price of $13.50 over the mean of Middle Eastern quotes for the one-year term that started in March 1997. The new price compares with a $7.90 premium for the term year that started in August 1996.
Following the initial round of bidding, the potential buyers are likely to have a face-to-face negotiation with Saudi Aramco probably in Singapore, traders said. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
